Reference / json

json#

JSON values: one immutable Json, parsed or built in code, read without casts and written by the runtime in one call.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let order = ParsedJson(text).root();
order.int("id");                                // 4711
order.get("customer").text("name");             // "Ada"
order.maybe("note").text() else "";                // "" when absent or null
let lines = order.list("items").map() -> line {
    Line(sku: line.text("sku"), qty: line.int("qty"));
};

let reply = Json(
    JsonField("id", 4711),
    JsonField("customer", Json(JsonField("name", "Ada"))),
    JsonField("tags", Json(items: [Json("new"), Json("vip")])),
);
reply.string();                                 // compact text
reply.pretty(2);                                // indented text

Description#

JSON values: one immutable Json, parsed or built in code, read without casts and written by the runtime in one call.

import "io/stdout" take Stdout;
let order = ParsedJson("{\"id\":4711}").root();
Stdout().writeln(order.int("id").string());
4711

Everything that goes wrong is a JsonError. Reads check kinds: a value of another kind is JsonError.wrong_kind, a missing member or index JsonError.missing, a number that is not the integer asked for JsonError.invalid_number; each names the RFC 6901 pointer of the value ("" is the root). Strict RFC 8259 parsing keeps member order, rejects repeated names (JsonError.duplicate_member_at) and nests at most 128 values deep unless told otherwise. Numbers are exact: Decimal, int or int, never float. Text output writes numbers positionally while that stays short (integers up to 21 digits, fractions down to 1e-6) and exactly otherwise.

Public API#

enum JsonKind#

enum JsonKind = (null_value, boolean_value, number_value, string_value, array_value, object_value)

Which of the six JSON kinds a value is.

  • null_value: JSON null.
  • boolean_value: A JSON boolean.
  • number_value: An exact JSON number.
  • string_value: A Unicode JSON string.
  • array_value: An ordered JSON array.
  • object_value: A JSON object with unique member names.

object JsonItems#

object JsonItems

JSON items read as a stream gives them (#136), one at a time with bounded memory: the elements of one top-level array, or values one after another (NDJSON, or any whitespace between them).

for await JsonItems(origin: upload) -> item {
    item.text("name");
}

A stream whose first significant byte is "[" is one array; its elements are the items. Each item is parsed whole as ParsedJson parses bytes, so its errors are JsonError.invalid with offsets inside the item; a broken stream is JsonError.invalid at its byte offset in the stream, line and column 0. An item may be 16 MiB and 128 levels deep unless told otherwise.

Errors#

enum JsonError#

enum JsonError is Error = (wrong_kind(pointer is string, expected is JsonKind, actual is JsonKind), missing(pointer is string), invalid_number(pointer is string, spelling is string, reason is string), invalid(offset is int, line is int, column is int, message is string), duplicate_member(name is string), duplicate_member_at(name is string, offset is int, line is int, column is int), invalid_indentation(amount is int))

What goes wrong with JSON; reads name the RFC 6901 pointer of the value.

  • wrong_kind: The value at pointer has actual kind instead of expected.
  • missing: No value exists at the RFC 6901 pointer.
  • invalid_number: The number at pointer cannot represent the requested type; spelling and reason explain the refusal.
  • invalid: Invalid JSON text, with zero-based byte offset and one-based line and column, plus a message.
  • duplicate_member: Building an object supplied the same member name more than once.
  • duplicate_member_at: Parsing found a repeated name, with its byte offset and one-based line and column.
  • invalid_indentation: Pretty-print indentation must be nonnegative; amount was refused.
